flashcard_questions.q: In which year did Elizabeth become Queen of England?
In which year did the Reformation begin in Europe?
Who nailed 95 complaints to a church door in 1517?
What did the Act of Supremacy make Elizabeth?
flashcard_questions.a: Supreme Governor of the Church of England.

flashcard_questions.q: Why was the title “Governor” chosen instead of “Head”?
flashcard_questions.a: It was less offensive to Catholics, who believed only Christ could head the Church.

flashcard_questions.q: Which prayer book did the Act of Uniformity make compulsory?
What fine did the Act of Uniformity set for missing Sunday church?
What Protestant change did the Settlement bring into church services?
flashcard_questions.a: They were now held in English.

flashcard_questions.q: What were the Royal Injunctions of 1559?
flashcard_questions.a: Instructions on how the Church should be run.

flashcard_questions.q: Which book did the Royal Injunctions require in every church?
Which term means fines for refusing to attend Church of England services?
What did the Pope do to Elizabeth in 1570?
flashcard_questions.a: He excommunicated her, cutting her off from the Catholic Church.

flashcard_questions.q: Which massacre of 1572 killed thousands of French Protestants?
Who built Elizabeth’s network of spies and double agents?

notes: 14 cards: 4 event/date, 4 term-to-definition (recusancy fines phrased 'Which term means...'), 3 person, 3 cause-effect. Both glossary terms used once only, in one direction.
